extraction_scope: worker-6 source-reviewed replacement of automated pending-review mechanism notes with bounded source-located claims.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Guavanin 2 is bactericidal against E. coli but with slow killing kinetics at twofold MIC rather than rapid sterilization.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=6:Guavanin 2 kills bacteria with slow membranolytic kinetics; xml:fig=2:Fig. 2

mechanism_claims.limitations: Time-kill supports bactericidal kinetics but does not by itself define a molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SYTOX Green uptake and DiSC3(5) assays support gradual membrane permeabilization with membrane hyperpolarization in E. coli.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=6:Guavanin 2 kills bacteria with slow membranolytic kinetics; xml:fig=2:Fig. 2

mechanism_claims.limitations: The source frames hyperpolarization as consistent with selective ionophore-like behavior; do not overclaim a resolved pore structure or ion specificity beyond the paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM-FEG imaging supports peptide-induced bacterial membrane damage in P. aeruginosa and L. ivanovii at MIC and twofold-MIC exposure.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Guavanin 2 against P. aeruginosa and L. ivanovii
mechanism_claims.limitations: SEM-FEG supports membrane damage morphology but not exact quantitative permeabilization rates.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD/NMR source evidence supports an alpha-helical Guavanin 2 conformation in hydrophobic or membrane-like environments, providing structural support for membrane interaction.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=9:Guavanin 2 structure depends on environment hydrophobicity; xml:fig=4:Fig. 4; xml:table=2

mechanism_claims.limitations: Structural support is not promoted to a separate direct killing mechanism without the membrane assays above.
